# Rosemary West

## Overview

- **Age:** At least 35 years old  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P0](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c2 P63](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0063)</sub>
- **Role:** music teacher  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050)</sub>
- **Titles:** sweet woman  <sub>[v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosemary is a tall, fair, and placid woman with a high white forehead, a finely shaped face, and pink cheeks. Her warm golden hair, which is the colour of new molasses taffy, is worn in sleek, close coils over her head. She has large, tranquil blue eyes full of friendliness, and is noted for her slow, sweet smile.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P52](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0052), [v5 c13 P7](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0007), [v5 c13 P8](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0008), [v5 c14 P39](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0039), [v5 c20 P9](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0009)_

## Personality

Rosemary is exceptionally sweet, charming, patient, and understanding, possessing a high-bred and stately air without appearing stuck-up. She retains a youthful, delighted surprise towards life that brings a feeling of youth to those around her. She shows great sympathy and forgiveness, often understanding others when most people do not.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P65](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0065), [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P9](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0009), [v5 c20 P9](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0009), [v5 c30 P26](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0026)_

## History

At seventeen, Rosemary became engaged to Martin Crawford beside a wild wood spring in Rainbow Valley, but he drowned shortly after when his ship was wrecked. Following her mother's death, Rosemary pledged a solemn vow with her sister Ellen over their mother's Bible never to marry and always to live together. She spent years staying close at home, occasionally giving music lessons to local children like Di and Nan Blythe because she enjoyed it. Rosemary encountered John Meredith by the hidden spring in Rainbow Valley and developed a close, affectionate bond with him. When John proposed marriage, she realized she loved him deeply but felt bound by her past vow to Ellen. Unable to decline in person, she wrote him a cold, formal refusal to extinguish his hopes. To cope with the emotional strain, she spent two months away visiting Kingsport. Upon returning, she continued to hold painful feelings for John while privately keeping her understanding and kindly nature toward his children.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c4 P50](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0050), [v5 c13 P0](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0000), [v5 c13 P6](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0006), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P24](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0024), [v5 c21 P28](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0028), [v5 c21 P29](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0029), [v5 c22 P41](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0041), [v5 c26 P15](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0015), [v5 c34 P23](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0023)_

## Quotes

> Will you let me have it? You made it so knackily. I never saw anyone make a birch cup so since my little brother used to make them long ago—before he died.  <sub>[v5 c13 P15](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0015)</sub>

> There is no need of my either forgetting or remembering it. You forget that I’m an old maid, Ellen. It is only your sisterly delusion that I am still young and blooming and dangerous. Mr. Meredith merely wants to be a friend—if he wants that much itself. He’ll forget us both long before he gets back to the manse.  <sub>[v5 c13 P35](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0035)</sub>

> No, it wasn’t. Not a bit fair. I remember I had a pet hen when I was a little girl. She was such a pretty little thing—all golden brown and speckly. I loved her as much as I ever loved any pet. She was never killed—she died of old age. Mother wouldn’t have her killed because she was my pet.  <sub>[v5 c20 P24](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0024)</sub>

> Ellen, I love John Meredith—I want to be his wife. Will you set me free from that promise?  <sub>[v5 c22 P21](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0021)</sub>
